rules.statement: Define a rule or pattern (such as a regex) once within a script or file and call it from every place that needs it, rather than declaring copies of it in separate functions or loops.
rules.why: Copies kept in step only by a comment drift apart, so one code path accepts input that another rejects.
rules.check: Look for the same regex, filter condition or exclusion list declared more than once in one file under different names or inline in several functions.

rules.statement: When the same rule must be duplicated across components that can't share code (for example a script that ships alone and can't import a module), add a parity test that runs both copies over the same real input and fails if they disagree.
rules.why: Without a test comparing them, the copies drift silently and the two components disagree, for example one accepts a name the other then rejects.
rules.check: Look for logic copied between two files, with a comment such as 'keep in sync', and no test comparing the outputs of both copies.

rules.statement: When a behaviour such as deduplication is added to a specific code path, cover it with a test that runs that path end to end, not only with a unit test of a helper on another path.
rules.why: If the behaviour regressed on the untested path, no test would fail.
rules.check: For new logic like `Select-Object -Unique` or `Distinct()` on an input path, check that some test feeds that path input that triggers it (such as a duplicate) and checks the result.

rules.statement: Wrap help text and documentation comment paragraphs to the width of the surrounding lines, with no line longer than 120 characters.
rules.why: One line running far past the paragraph's width makes the help text harder to read.
rules.check: Look in rewrapped or edited comment-based help (.DESCRIPTION and similar) or doc comments for a line much longer than its neighbours or over 120 characters.
